messages:
Maria G: quick flag — noticed a spike in eval deltas for the structured-output suite after the quant-mix deploy (fp8 + int4 path). lots of small hallucinations and a few JSON parse failures. reproducible on staging and one customer report on prod.
Ken T: oof, saw a couple alerts this morning. any specific model/version?
Maria G: r-infer/sea-13.1 (mixed-quant build with new kernel selector). diffs show token-level drift starting around step ~42 in outputs. sample: expected '{\"items\": []}' vs got '{\"items\": null, \"note\": \"processed\"}' which breaks downstream parsers.
Alex R: can you paste a minimal repro prompt and the eval id? I can run a local quant-run with profile enabled.
Maria G: eval id 2027-QUANT-38. repro prompt (trimmed):
```
Generate a JSON array of 3 user objects with id, name, and roles.
```
Ken T: thanks. when you say "kernel selector" was updated — we flipped the heuristic to prefer fp8 kernels for QKV matmuls even when activations are int4 to save memory. maybe the kernel cross-precision path introduces small numerics.
Sophie L: telemetry from the run: p50 latency unchanged, p99 +8% on staging for mixed-quant. throughput stable. perf profile shows increased time in kernel-copy and quant-dequant ops. attaching snippet: `kernel_selector=fp8_pref; batcher=adaptive_v2; kv_cache_prefetch=on`
infra-bot: deploy 2472098000 to infer-prod completed by ci/deploy-bot — image: r-infer:v13.1-quantmix-202703.
Jack O: I can bisect on the runtime side. suspect commit 7f3c2b9 (adaptive kernel steering) or the calibration changes that changed per-layer scale.
Alex R: ran eval locally with and without the new kernel selector. without selector (force old kernel) outputs match baseline. with selector enabled, small token substitutions occur which lead to structural differences. indicates numerical noise crossing threshold checks in our tokenizer->postprocess logic.
Maria G: interesting — also saw KV cache warmup differences. when KV cache is cold the first few tokens diverge, and divergence persists. could be cache write order or dtype mishandling.
Ken T: any stack traces or logs showing dtype casts? we added a new fast-path where we memcpy int4 to fp8 workspace in place for speed. if that path has off-by-one or alignment issues could corrupt KV.
Sophie L: profiling heap shows occasional misaligned writes on the fp8 workspace on ampere nodes. sample trace:
```
trace: kernel:fast_promote_fp8 memcpy len=10240 dst=0x7f8a ... (unaligned)
err_rate: 0.002
```
Alex R: can we run a repro with --no-kv-prefetch and --force-legacy-kernel to narrow down?
Maria G: doing that now in staging. also running the quant-calib job with previous calibration artifacts (pre-change) to see if calibration delta is the culprit.
(5m later)
Maria G: quick update — forcing legacy kernel removes the JSON breaks and hallucinations. disabling kv_prefetch reduces p99 but doesn't remove structural errors entirely. calibration rollback reduces the hallucination rate by ~70% but not fully.
Ken T: implies two orthogonal issues: 1) kernel selector path introduces small numeric diffs that can flip structural predicates, 2) calibration change amplifies those diffs.
Sophie L: for triage: run matrix: [legacy/selector] x [old-calib/new-calib] x [kv_prefetch on/off] and record eval delta and p99. I'll tap telemetry to automatically generate the matrix runs.
Alex R: I'll add assertions to structured-output postproc to be more robust temporarily (e.g., coerce null->[] for specific keys) to buy time for a patch. but we should fix root cause.
Jack O: I'll start a bisection on 7f3c2b9..a4d11cc to isolate kernel selector change. any suspicious PRs in calibration? (cc @Sophie L)
Sophie L: calibration changes came from PR #5124 (per-layer epsilon tweak) — that made some layers' scales slightly smaller. combined with fp8 promotion that could overflow/underflow in a way that moves tokens.
Maria G: agreed. immediate mitigation: revert kernel selector to legacy for the mixed-quant rollout and pin calibration artifact to pre-PR #5124 for the next batch of canaries.
Ken T: let's coordinate rollback window. I can schedule a rollback to 2472098000 image for the night canary at 22:00 UTC if we all ack.
Maria G: ack. also posting a short note to the release channel to pause further canaries.
Sophie L: I'll attach the matrix results and a short root-cause blurb once the bisection and matrix complete.
Alex R: follow-ups: add more numeric tolerance tests in eval harness, run long tail with varied prompt lengths (some failures are length-dependent), and add alignment checks in the memcpy path.
Jack O: logging plan: temporary extra checks in kernel fast-path to detect misaligned writes and dump small binary snapshot when detected. will throttle dumps.
Maria G: thanks all. if anyone sees customer tickets referencing parse errors, ping here. we'll reopen canary after rollback + fixes. :thumbsup:
